transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Um… yeah, I guess the main reason I’m here is that I’ve realized I’m planning way too much of my life around avoiding elevators. Like, it sounds kind of silly when I say it out loud, but it’s started getting in the way.

At home I’ve been taking five flights of stairs instead of using the elevator, even when I’m tired or carrying stuff. And for work, I turned down this workshop because it was in a high-rise building, and I just kept thinking about the elevator situation instead of the actual training. I also stopped visiting one of my older computer students, which I feel pretty bad about, because his building doesn’t really have another good option besides the elevator.

So… I think that’s what made me feel like I should talk to someone, because I’m not just disliking elevators anymore. I’m kind of arranging things so I don’t have to deal with them.
What is it about elevators that feels frightening to you?

It’s mostly this fear that I’m going to be stuck in there, or that something mechanical is going to fail. Like… I know, logically, if it’s an elevator in an office building, it’s probably inspected and safe and people use it all day without anything happening. I do understand that.

But when I’m actually standing there looking at the doors, especially the older ones in my apartment building or at work, my brain doesn’t treat it like a normal elevator. It’s more like, “If you get in, you might not get back out,” or, “What if it drops?” Even saying that, I know it sounds kind of dramatic, because obviously elevators aren’t just dropping all the time. But in the moment it feels very real, like I’m about to step into a trap or something.
Have you ever had a panic attack that came out of nowhere, not just when you were around an elevator?

Um… no, I don’t think so. At least not that I can remember in the way you’re describing, like totally out of nowhere.

When I get really worked up, it’s pretty much connected to the elevator thing, or even just thinking ahead about having to use one. I don’t really have episodes where I’m just sitting at home or at work and suddenly feel panicky for no reason. I mean, I get stressed like anyone, but not that sudden kind of attack out of the blue.
Do unwanted thoughts about elevators keep popping into your mind even when you’re trying not to think about them?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I don’t think it’s like… random thoughts popping in all day when I’m trying to think about something else, if that’s what you mean.

It’s more that if I know I might have to deal with an elevator, then I’ll start thinking about it a lot. Like if I’m going somewhere and I’m not sure what floor it’s on, my mind goes there pretty quickly. But if I’m just at home doing something unrelated or talking to someone, I’m not usually having elevator thoughts just barge in out of nowhere.

So I guess I’d say not really unwanted thoughts in that intrusive way, or at least I haven’t noticed it like that. It’s more tied to situations where elevators might actually come up.
Are elevators the only thing you avoid because of this kind of fear?

Mostly elevators, yeah. I mean, that’s the thing I’m really organizing around. It’s not like I’m avoiding a whole bunch of different things in the same way.

The elevator thing has started spilling into my day more than I’d like to admit. Like at home, I’ll take the stairs even though it’s five flights, and I kind of pretend that’s just “good exercise,” but honestly it’s because I don’t want to get in the elevator. And with work, I turned down this workshop because it was in a high-rise, and I just didn’t want to deal with figuring out if I’d have to use one or how many floors it was or whether stairs would even be realistic.

And there’s this older computer student I used to visit, and I’ve basically stopped going because his building doesn’t really have another option. That one makes me feel especially bad, because it affects someone else too, not just me being inconvenienced. So… yeah, it’s specifically elevators, but I’m definitely avoiding things because of them.
